verdict.rationale: Checkout.com explicitly documents idempotency support across all key mutating endpoints (payments, authorizations, captures, refunds, voids, transfers) via a `Cko-Idempotency-Key` header, caching successful (2xx) responses and offering a configurable idempotency window to prevent duplicate charges from retried requests. This directly and precisely matches the story. Missing for 10: no independent/hands-on third-party corroboration of behavior beyond first-party docs.
